definition: Magnanimous means great-souled: generous and forgiving toward a rival or wrongdoer, especially when you hold the upper hand and have every right to be petty.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word magnanimous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know magnanimous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: In a magnanimous gesture nobody expected, the winning architect asked the jury to publish her rival's design alongside her own.
Gracious is milder than magnanimous: graciousness is warm good manners toward anyone, while magnanimity forgives a real injury from a real rival — it gives up something the giver was owed.
Saintly goes further than magnanimous — the magnanimous winner forgives the rival standing in front of them, while the saintly forgive everyone, everywhere, and keep no ledger at all.

Generous is the everyday word for giving freely — money, time, second helpings — to anyone at all. Magnanimous narrows and elevates it: generosity of spirit shown to a rival or a wrongdoer, from the position where pettiness would have been easy.

Forgiving lets an injury go, and anyone can do it from any position. Magnanimous adds the seat of power: the winner or the wronged party who could exact a price chooses instead to be openhanded about it — forgiveness with a gift on top.
small-minded about slights and scorekeeping
bent on paying every injury back
After an hour of debate, the zoning board's vote came back unanimous, and the clerk read the result aloud twice to be sure.
Magnanimous means great-souled: generous and forgiving toward a rival or wrongdoer, especially when you hold the upper hand and have every right to be petty.

After the tennis final, the seventeen-year-old champion was magnanimous at the net and afterward: she told reporters the tournament's best shot had been her opponent's, and she asked the club to split her exhibition fee with the runner-up's academy.
Magnanimity is generosity exercised from the winner's seat.
She holds every advantage and owes her rival nothing — the moment invites gloating — and she spends it lifting the person she just beat.
That upward gift from a position of strength is what separates magnanimous from ordinary kindness.
Magnanimous is praise with a precondition: the speaker believes you had the power to punish and the right to gloat, and you chose neither.
Call an everyday giver generous; save magnanimous for the winner's gesture toward the loser, or the wronged party's grace toward the offender.
Its root-cousin unanimous (met in the root check above) shares only the spirit — animus — not the size.

The recount took nine days, and by the end of it Mayor-elect Iris Chen had heard her opponent question her honesty on every call-in show in the county.
She won by ninety-one votes.

At her first council meeting, Chen proposed that Tomas Vega — the man who had demanded the recount and implied she had rigged it — lead the new flood-levee commission, the project his own campaign had been built around.
Her staff objected that she owed Vega nothing, and less than nothing.
'That is what makes it worth doing,' she said.
Even the county paper, which had endorsed Vega, called the appointment magnanimous, and noted that the levee was the one issue on which he was undeniably the better engineer.
